You are sandy_walnut42, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with gentle_otter27, pale_lantern48, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.

I’ll inspect the bundled docs and probe the CLI’s main behaviors first, then implement the common paths and compare outputs. I’ll also check the group channel for an existing overview so I can coordinate around what teammates are covering.

See for yourself at the [W3C Validator](http://validator.w3.org/)!* Minify is a minifier package written in [Go][1]. It provides HTML5, CSS3, JS, JSON, SVG and XML minifiers and an interface to implement any other minifier. Minification is the process of removing bytes from a file (such as whitespace) without changing its output and therefore shrinking its size and speeding up transmission over the internet and possibly parsing. The implemented minifiers are designed for high performance (see https://github.com/privatenumber/minification-benchmarks where this library is (one of) the fastest JS minifiers). The core functionality associates mimetypes with minification functions, allowing embedded resources (like CSS or JS within HTML files) to be minified as well. Users can add new implementations that are triggered based on a mimetype (or pattern), or redirect to an external command (like ClosureCompiler, UglifyCSS, ...). ### Sponsors #### SiteGround [![SiteGround](https://www.siteground.com/img/downloads/siteground-logo-black-transparent-vector.svg)](https://www.siteground.com/) Thank you SiteGround for having sponsored this project for many years! Please see the Sponsors button in GitHub for ways to contribute, or contact me directly. #### Table of Contents - [Minify](#minify) - [Prologue](#prologue) - [Installation](#installation) - [API stability](#api-stability) - [Testing](#testing) - [Performance](#performance) - [HTML](#html) - [Whitespace removal](#whitespace-removal) - [CSS](#css) - [JS](#js) - [Comparison with other tools](#comparison-with-other-tools) - [Compression ratio (lower is better)](#compression-ratio-lower-is-better) - [Time (lower is better)](#time-lower-is-better) - [JSON](#json) - [SVG](#svg) - [XML](#xml) - [Usage](#usage) - [New](#new) - [From reader](#from-reader) - [From bytes](#from-bytes) - [From string](#from-string) - [To reader](#to-reader) - [To writer](#to-writer) - [Middleware](#middleware) - [Custom minifier](#custom-minifier) - [Mediatypes](#mediatypes) - [Examples](#examples) - [Common minifiers](#common-minifiers) - [External minifiers](#external-minifiers) - [Closure Compiler](#closure-compiler) - [UglifyJS](#uglifyjs) - [esbuild](#esbuild) - [Custom minifier](#custom-minifier-example) - [ResponseWriter](#responsewriter) - [Templates](#templates) - [FAQ](#faq) - [License](#license) ### Roadmap - [ ] Use ASM/SSE to further speed-up core parts of the parsers/minifiers - [x] Improve JS minifiers by shortening variables and proper semicolon omission - [ ] Speed-up SVG minifier, it is very slow - [x] Proper parser error reporting and line number + column information - [ ] Generation of source maps (uncertain, might slow down parsers too much if it cannot run separately nicely) - [ ] Create a cmd to pack webfiles (much like webpack), ie. merging CSS and JS files, inlining small external files, minification and gzipping. This would work on HTML files. ## Prologue Minifiers or bindings to minifiers exist in almost all programming languages. Some implementations are merely using several regular expressions to trim whitespace and comments (even though regex for parsing HTML/XML is ill-advised, for a good read see [Regular Expressions: Now You Have Two Problems](http://blog.codinghorror.com/regular-expressions-now-you-have-two-problems/)). Some implementations are much more profound, such as the [YUI Compressor](http://yui.github.io/yuicompressor/) and [Google Closure Compiler](https://github.com/google/closure-compiler) for JS. As most existing implementations either use JavaScript, use regexes, and don't focus on performance, they are pretty slow. This minifier proves to be that fast and extensive minifier that can handle HTML and any other filetype it may contain (CSS, JS, ...). It is usually orders of magnitude faster than existing minifiers. ## Installation Make sure you have [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and [Go](https://golang.org/dl/) (1.18 or higher) installed, run ``` mkdir Project cd Project go mod init go get -u github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2 ``` Then add the following imports to be able to use the various minifiers ``` go import ( "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/css" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/html" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/js" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/json" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/svg" "github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/xml" ) ``` You can optionally run `go mod tidy` to clean up the `go.mod` and `go.sum` files. See [CLI tool](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/tree/master/cmd/minify) for installation instructions of the binary. ### Docker If you want to use Docker, please see https://hub.docker.com/r/tdewolff/minify. ```bash $ docker run -it tdewolff/minify --help ``` ## API stability There is no guarantee for absolute stability, but I take issues and bugs seriously and don't take API changes lightly. The library will be maintained in a compatible way unless vital bugs prevent me from doing so. There has been one API change after v1 which added options support and I took the opportunity to push through some more API clean up as well. There are no plans whatsoever for future API changes. ## Testing For all subpackages and the imported `parse` package, test coverage of 100% is pursued. Besides full coverage, the minifiers are [fuzz tested](https://github.com/tdewolff/fuzz) using [github.com/dvyukov/go-fuzz](http://www.github.com/dvyukov/go-fuzz), see [the wiki](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/wiki) for the most important bugs found by fuzz testing. These tests ensure that everything works as intended and that the code does not crash (whatever the input). If you still encounter a bug, please file a [bug report](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/issues)! ## Performance The benchmarks directory contains a number of standardized samples used to compare performance between changes. The JS minifier typically shaves off about 35% -- 65% of filesize depending on the file, which is a compression close to many other minifiers. Common speeds of PHP and JS implementations are about 100-300kB/s (see [Uglify2](http://lisperator.net/uglifyjs/), [Adventures in PHP web asset minimization](https://www.happyassassin.net/2014/12/29/adventures-in-php-web-asset-minimization/)). This implementation is orders of magnitude faster at around ~25MB/s.

The following features are implemented:

- remove superfluous whitespace
- remove superfluous semicolons
- shorten `true`, `false`, and `undefined` to `!0`, `!1` and `void 0`
- rename variables and functions to shorter names (not in global scope)
- move `var` declarations to the top of the global/function scope (if more than one)
- collapse if/else statements to expressions
- minify conditional expressions to simpler ones
- merge sequential expression statements to one, including into `return` and `throw`
- remove superfluous grouping in expressions
- shorten or remove string escapes
- convert object key or index expression from string to identifier or decimal
- merge concatenated strings
- rewrite numbers (binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal) to shorter representations

Options:

- `KeepVarNames` keeps variable names as they are and omits shortening variable names
- `Precision` number of significant digits to preserve for numbers, `0` means no trimming
- `Version` ECMAScript version to use for output, `0` is the latest

### Comparison with other tools

Performance is measured with `time [command]` ran 10 times and selecting the fastest one, on a Thinkpad T460 (i5-6300U quad-core 2.4GHz running Arch Linux) using Go 1.15.

- [minify](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify): `minify -o script.min.js script.js`
- [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild): `esbuild --minify --outfile=script.min.js script.js`
- [terser](https://github.com/terser/terser): `terser script.js --compress --mangle -o script.min.js`
- [UglifyJS](https://github.com/Skalman/UglifyJS-online): `uglifyjs --compress --mangle -o script.min.js script.js`
- [Closure Compiler](https://github.com/google/closure-compiler): `closure-compiler -O SIMPLE --js script.js --js_output_file script.min.js --language_in ECMASCRIPT_NEXT -W QUIET --jscomp_off=checkVars` optimization level `SIMPLE` instead of `ADVANCED` to make similar assumptions as do the other tools (do not rename/assume anything of global level variables)

#### Compression ratio (lower is better)
All tools give very similar results, although UglifyJS compresses slightly better.

| Tool | ace.js | dot.js | jquery.js | jqueryui.js | moment.js |

#### Time (lower is better)
Most tools are extremely slow, with `minify` and `esbuild` being orders of magnitudes faster.

## JSON

Minification typically shaves off about 15% of filesize for common indented JSON such as generated by [JSON Generator](http://www.json-generator.com/).

The JSON minifier only removes whitespace, which is the only thing that can be left out, and minifies numbers (`1000` => `1e3`).

Options:

- `Precision` number of significant digits to preserve for numbers, `0` means no trimming
- `KeepNumbers` do not minify numbers if set to `true`, by default numbers will be minified

## SVG

The SVG minifier uses these minifications:

- trim and collapse whitespace between all tags
- strip comments, empty `doctype`, XML prelude, `metadata`
- strip SVG version
- strip CDATA sections wherever possible
- collapse tags with no content to a void tag
- minify style tag and attributes with the CSS minifier
- minify colors
- shorten lengths and numbers and remove default `px` unit
- shorten `path` data
- use relative or absolute positions in path data whichever is shorter

Options:

- `KeepComments` preserve comments
- `KeepNamespaces` a list of XML namespace prefixes to preserve, default is `[]string{"xlink"}`
- `Precision` number of significant digits to preserve for numbers, `0` means no trimming

## XML

The XML minifier uses these minifications:

- strip unnecessary whitespace and otherwise collapse it to one space (or newline if it originally contained a newline)
- strip comments
- collapse tags with no content to a void tag
- strip CDATA sections wherever possible

Options:

- `KeepWhitespace` preserve whitespace between inline tags but still collapse multiple whitespace characters into one

## Usage
Any input stream is being buffered by the minification functions. This is how the underlying buffer package inherently works to ensure high performance. The output stream however is not buffered. It is wise to preallocate a buffer as big as the input to which the output is written, or otherwise use `bufio` to buffer to a streaming writer.

import re

# A conservative CSS token pass: preserve strings and comments while removing
# insignificant whitespace and applying common safe value reductions.
def _scan(s):
    out=[]; i=0; n=len(s)
    while i<n:
        c=s[i]
        if c in "\"'":
            q=c; j=i+1
            while j<n:
                if s[j]=='\\': j+=2; continue
                if s[j]==q: j+=1; break
                j+=1
            out.append(('str',s[i:j])); i=j
        elif s.startswith('/*',i):
            j=s.find('*/',i+2); j=n if j<0 else j+2
            comment=s[i:j]
            if comment.startswith('/*!'): out.append(('keep',comment))
            else: out.append(('comment',''))
            i=j
        else: out.append(('char',c)); i+=1
    return out

def minify_css(text, precision=0, version=0):
    toks=_scan(text)
    # Normalize token values and collapse whitespace. A space remains only
    # between adjacent word-like tokens or when required by selector syntax.
    raw=''.join(v for _,v in toks)
    raw=re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', raw)
    # Strip comments (including spaces left adjacent to them).
    raw=re.sub(r'/\*(?!\!)[\s\S]*?\*/','',raw)
    raw=re.sub(r'\s*([{}:;,>+~])\s*',r'\1',raw)
    raw=re.sub(r'\s*\(\s*','(',raw); raw=re.sub(r'\s*\)\s*',')',raw)
    raw=re.sub(r'\s+', ' ',raw).strip()
    raw=raw.replace(';}', '}')
    # Comments retained by license convention lose internal edge spaces.
    raw=re.sub(r'/\*!\s*([\s\S]*?)\s*\*/',r'/*!\1*/',raw)
    raw=re.sub(r'(\*/)[ ]+',r'\1',raw)
    # Number cleanup including zero dimensions and leading zeros.
    def num(m):
        x=m.group(0)
        x=re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])\+','',x)
        x=re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])0+(\d)',r'\1',x)
        x=re.sub(r'(\d)\.0+(?=[a-z%]|\b)',r'\1',x,flags=re.I)
        x=re.sub(r'(\d+\.\d*?[1-9])0+(?=[a-zA-Z%]|$)',r'\1',x)
        x=re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])0\.(\d+)',r'.\1',x)
        if re.match(r'^0(?:px|em|rem|%|pt|pc|in|cm|mm|ex|ch|vh|vw|vmin|vmax)$',x,re.I): x='0'
        return x
    raw=re.sub(r'(?<![-\w])\+?(?:\d*\.)?\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?(?:[a-zA-Z%]+)?',num,raw)
    # Lowercase ordinary identifiers; preserve selector ids/classes and strings.
    # Broad transform values after declaration colon, avoiding URLs.
    def decl(m):
        prop=m.group(1).lower(); val=m.group(2)
        val=re.sub(r'(?i)\bnormal\b','400',val) if prop in ('font','font-weight') else val
        if prop in ('font','font-weight'): val=re.sub(r'(?i)\bbold\b','700',val)
        if prop in ('margin','padding','border-width'):
            a=val.split()
            if len(a)==4 and a[0]==a[2] and a[1]==a[3]: a=a[:2]
            if len(a)==3 and a[0]==a[2]: a=a[:2]
            if len(a)==2 and a[0]==a[1]: a=a[:1]
            val=' '.join(a)
        return prop+':'+val
    raw=re.sub(r'([\w-]+):([^;{}]*)',decl,raw)
    # Canonical colors, short hex colors.
    raw=re.sub(r'(?i)#([0-9a-f])\1([0-9a-f])\2([0-9a-f])\3\b',r'#\1\2\3',raw)
    colors={'#ffffff':'#fff','#000000':'#000','#ff0000':'red','#0000ff':'#00f','#ffff00':'#ff0','#008000':'green','#800000':'maroon','#808080':'gray','#c0c0c0':'silver','#00ffff':'#0ff','#ff00ff':'#f0f'}
    for a,b in colors.items(): raw=re.sub(a+r'\b',b,raw,flags=re.I)
    raw=re.sub(r'(?i)\brgb\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)',lambda m: colors.get('#%02x%02x%02x'%(int(m[1]),int(m[2]),int(m[3])), '#%02x%02x%02x'%(int(m[1]),int(m[2]),int(m[3]))),raw)
    raw=re.sub(r'(?i)(border|background|outline):none',r'\1:0',raw)
    # Drop whitespace before !important but retain whitespace between tokens.
    raw=re.sub(r'\s*!important','!important',raw,flags=re.I)
    return raw

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/jsmin.py
+"""Conservative JavaScript token minifier used by the CLI."""
+import re
+
+_OPS = ("===", "!==", ">>>", "**=", "...", "=>", "==", "!=", "<=", ">=",
+        "++", "--", "&&", "||", "??", "?.", "+=", "-=", "*=", "/=",
+        "**", "<<", ">>", "&=", "|=", "??=")
+
+def minify_js(source, precision=0, keep_var_names=False, version=0):
+    out=[]; i=0; n=len(source); prev=''; can_regex=True
+    while i<n:
+        c=source[i]
+        if c.isspace():
+            j=i+1
+            while j<n and source[j].isspace(): j+=1
+            nxt=source[j] if j<n else ''
+            if prev and nxt and ((prev[-1].isalnum() or prev[-1] in '_$') and (nxt.isalnum() or nxt in '_$')):
+                out.append(' ')
+            i=j; continue
+        if source.startswith('//',i):
+            j=source.find('\n',i+2); i=n if j<0 else j+1; continue
+        if source.startswith('/*',i):
+            j=source.find('*/',i+2); j=n if j<0 else j+2
+            if source.startswith('/*!',i):
+                out.append(source[i:j]); prev=source[i:j]
+            i=j; continue
+        if c in "'\"`":
+            q=c; j=i+1
+            while j<n:
+                if source[j]=='\\': j+=2; continue
+                if source[j]==q: j+=1; break
+                j+=1
+            token=source[i:min(j,n)]; out.append(token); prev=token; can_regex=False; i=j; continue
+        if c.isalpha() or c in '_$':
+            j=i+1
+            while j<n and (source[j].isalnum() or source[j] in '_$'): j+=1
+            word=source[i:j]
+            token={'true':'!0','false':'!1','undefined':'void 0'}.get(word,word)
+            out.append(token); prev=token
+            can_regex=word in ('return','throw','case','delete','typeof','void','new','in','of','yield','await','else')
+            i=j; continue
+        if c.isdigit() or (c=='.' and i+1<n and source[i+1].isdigit()):
+            m=re.match(r'(?:0[xX][\da-fA-F]+|0[bB][01]+|0[oO][0-7]+|(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)',source[i:])
+            token=m.group(0) if m else c
+            if precision:
+                try: token=format(float(token),'.%dg'%precision)
+                except (ValueError,OverflowError): pass
+            out.append(token); prev=token; can_regex=False; i+=len(m.group(0)) if m else 1; continue
+        if c=='/' and can_regex:
+            # Keep a regexp literal intact, including escaped slashes and classes.
+            j=i+1; in_class=False
+            while j<n:
+                if source[j]=='\\': j+=2; continue
+                if source[j]=='[': in_class=True
+                elif source[j]==']': in_class=False
+                elif source[j]=='/' and not in_class:
+                    j+=1
+                    while j<n and source[j].isalpha(): j+=1
+                    break
+                elif source[j] in '\r\n': break
+                j+=1
+            if j>i+1 and j<=n and '/' in source[i+1:j]:
+                token=source[i:j]; out.append(token); prev=token; can_regex=False; i=j; continue
+        op=next((x for x in _OPS if source.startswith(x,i)),c)
+        # Avoid changing ++x into + +x or x++ into x+ +.
+        if op in ('+','-') and prev and prev[-1] in '+-' and op==prev[-1]: out.append(' ')
+        out.append(op); prev=op
+        can_regex=op in ('(','[','{',',',';',':','=','!','?','return','=>')
+        i+=len(op)
+    result=''.join(out).strip()
+    result=re.sub(r';(?=[}\]])','',result)
+    return result
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r);

"""Conservative JavaScript token minifier used by the CLI."""
import re

_OPS = ("===", "!==", ">>>", "**=", "...", "=>", "==", "!=", "<=", ">=",
        "++", "--", "&&", "||", "??", "?.", "+=", "-=", "*=", "/=",
        "**", "<<", ">>", "&=", "|=", "??=")

def minify_js(source, precision=0, keep_var_names=False, version=0):
    out=[]; i=0; n=len(source); prev=''; can_regex=True
    while i<n:
        c=source[i]
        if c.isspace():
            j=i+1
            while j<n and source[j].isspace(): j+=1
            nxt=source[j] if j<n else ''
            if prev and nxt and ((prev[-1].isalnum() or prev[-1] in '_$') and (nxt.isalnum() or nxt in '_$')):
                out.append(' ')
            i=j; continue
        if source.startswith('//',i):
            j=source.find('\n',i+2); i=n if j<0 else j+1; continue
        if source.startswith('/*',i):
            j=source.find('*/',i+2); j=n if j<0 else j+2
            if source.startswith('/*!',i):
                out.append(source[i:j]); prev=source[i:j]
            i=j; continue
        if c in "'\"`":
            q=c; j=i+1
            while j<n:
                if source[j]=='\\': j+=2; continue
                if source[j]==q: j+=1; break
                j+=1
            token=source[i:min(j,n)]; out.append(token); prev=token; can_regex=False; i=j; continue
        if c.isalpha() or c in '_$':
            j=i+1
            while j<n and (source[j].isalnum() or source[j] in '_$'): j+=1
            word=source[i:j]
            token={'true':'!0','false':'!1','undefined':'void 0'}.get(word,word)
            out.append(token); prev=token
            can_regex=word in ('return','throw','case','delete','typeof','void','new','in','of','yield','await','else')
            i=j; continue
        if c.isdigit() or (c=='.' and i+1<n and source[i+1].isdigit()):
            m=re.match(r'(?:0[xX][\da-fA-F]+|0[bB][01]+|0[oO][0-7]+|(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)',source[i:])
            token=m.group(0) if m else c
            if precision:
                try: token=format(float(token),'.%dg'%precision)
                except (ValueError,OverflowError): pass
            out.append(token); prev=token; can_regex=False; i+=len(m.group(0)) if m else 1; continue
        if c=='/' and can_regex:
            # Keep a regexp literal intact, including escaped slashes and classes.
            j=i+1; in_class=False
            while j<n:
                if source[j]=='\\': j+=2; continue
                if source[j]=='[': in_class=True
                elif source[j]==']': in_class=False
                elif source[j]=='/' and not in_class:
                    j+=1
                    while j<n and source[j].isalpha(): j+=1
                    break
                elif source[j] in '\r\n': break
                j+=1
            if j>i+1 and j<=n and '/' in source[i+1:j]:
                token=source[i:j]; out.append(token); prev=token; can_regex=False; i=j; continue
        op=next((x for x in _OPS if source.startswith(x,i)),c)
        # Avoid changing ++x into + +x or x++ into x+ +.
        if op in ('+','-') and prev and prev[-1] in '+-' and op==prev[-1]: out.append(' ')
        out.append(op); prev=op
        can_regex=op in ('(','[','{',',',';',':','=','!','?','return','=>')
        i+=len(op)
    result=''.join(out).strip()
    result=re.sub(r';(?=[}\]])','',result)
    # Identifier-shaped object keys and bracket properties need no quotes.
    result=re.sub(r"(['\"])([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\1(?=\s*:)",r'\2',result)
    result=re.sub(r"\[(['\"])([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\1\]",r'.\2',result)
    # The parser can express a compact if/else as a conditional expression
    # when both branches are single statements.
    def conditional(m):
        yes=m.group(2).strip().rstrip(';')
        no=m.group(3).strip().rstrip(';')
        return m.group(1)+'?'+yes+':'+no
    result=re.sub(r'if\(([^(){}]+)\)\{([^{}]*)\}else\{([^{}]*)\}',conditional,result)
    # A final semicolon is never required at end of a JavaScript stream.
    result=result.rstrip(';')
    return result
